cards.title: Remotes
cards.body: GitHub keeps a copy of your repository online. A remote is Git's name for that copy; the usual name is `origin`.
cards.code:
git init
git remote add origin https://github.com/you/demo.git
git remote -v

cards.title: Creating the GitHub side
cards.body: On github.com you create an empty repository and copy its URL. In these lessons, that repository already exists for you.

check.question: What is `origin` in `git remote add origin <url>`?
options: A short name for the GitHub URL
check.explanation: After this, `origin` stands for the URL in every command.

exercise.prompt: An empty repository is waiting at `https://github.com/you/site.git`. Add it as a remote called `origin`.
